arguments.text: #1 is fixed: `dayjs.tz` now routes non-string inputs (timestamp, Date, Day.js object) through `dayjs(input).tz(timezone)` instead of the wall-clock string path, so `Parse parse timestamp, js Date, Day.js object` matches moment. Verified in TZ=Pacific/Auckland, Europe/London, America/Whitehorse and UTC (full suite green, 524 tests).
`ordinal: n => n` — it returns the number `n` unchanged.

#4 is fixed: `proto.tz` now rounds the computed offset difference (`Math.round`), so fractional minutes from millisecond inputs no longer leak into the offset (`format('Z')` is now `-04:00` instead of `-04:0.00833...`). Verified with sub-second inputs across timezones.

#8 is fixed: `src/locale/nl.js` `ordinal` now produces the Dutch ordinal (`1ste`, `2de`, `8ste`, `20ste`, `21ste`, `22de`…) instead of `1.`, `2.`, so `Format Day of Month Do 1 - 31` matches moment. Full jest suite still green (524 tests).

import dayjs from '../src'
import duration from '../src/plugin/duration'
import moment from 'moment'
dayjs.extend(duration)
it('Creating milliseconds', () => {
  expect(dayjs.duration(100).toISOString()).toBe('PT0.1S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1000).toISOString()).toBe('PT1S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds').toISOString()).toBe('PT0.1S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds').asMilliseconds()).toBe(100)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').asMilliseconds()).toBe(1)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'millisecond').asMilliseconds()).toBe(1)
  expect(dayjs.duration(500, 'milliseconds').milliseconds()).toBe(500)
  expect(dayjs.duration(1500, 'milliseconds').asMilliseconds()).toBe(1500)
})
it('compare with moment', () => {
  ;[[100, 'milliseconds'], [1, 'ms'], [100, 'ms'], [1, 'second'], [1, 'minute'], [1, 'hour'], [1, 'day'], [1, 'week'], [1, 'month'], [1, 'year']].forEach(([v, u]) => {
    expect(dayjs.duration(v, u).asMilliseconds()).toBe(moment.duration(v, u).asMilliseconds())
    expect(dayjs.duration(v, u).toISOString()).toBe(moment.duration(v, u).toISOString())
  })
})
EOF
